title: Macaroni or Pasta Salad with Egg

content.title: About
content.content: Macaroni or pasta salad with egg is a cold dish where cooked pasta (or macaroni) is mixed with hard‑boiled eggs, mayonnaise or yogurt, fresh vegetables and seasonings. It is popular as a light lunch, snack or picnic food.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Short‑shaped pasta such as rotini, penne or farfalle is commonly used because it holds the dressing well.
Eggs add not only flavor but also a complete set of proteins and vitamins.
Different countries use different dressings: in Russia – mayonnaise, in Italy – olive oil with lemon, in the US – a yogurt‑based sauce.
The salad can be prepared ahead of time and keeps well in the fridge for 2‑3 days.
Fresh herbs like parsley, dill or basil boost aroma and make the dish more vibrant.

items.title: Rich in protein
items.content: Eggs and pasta provide high‑quality protein essential for tissue growth and repair.

items.title: Energy source
items.content: Carbohydrates from pasta give a quick source of energy, making the salad a good pre‑exercise option.

items.title: B‑vitamins
items.content: Eggs contain vitamin B12, while whole‑grain pasta supplies B1, B2, B3, supporting metabolism.

items.title: Minerals
items.content: The dish provides iron, phosphorus and selenium from eggs and magnesium from pasta, supporting nervous system function.

items.title: Digestive benefits
items.content: Adding fresh vegetables (cucumber, tomato, green onion) increases fiber, promoting healthy digestion.

items.title: Egg allergy
items.content: Some individuals may experience allergic reactions to eggs, ranging from skin rashes to anaphylaxis.

items.title: Cholesterol content
items.content: Eggs are high in cholesterol; people with elevated cholesterol levels should limit their intake.

items.title: Food poisoning risk
items.content: Improperly cooked or stored eggs can harbor salmonella; use fresh eggs and keep the salad refrigerated.

items.title: Gluten
items.content: Traditional pasta contains gluten, so those with celiac disease should use gluten‑free alternatives (rice or corn pasta).

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Serve the salad chilled, often in individual bowls or cups. It can be eaten on its own, with bread or crackers, or as a side dish to meat or fish.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep the salad in an airtight container in the refrigerator at 0‑4 °C. It remains tasty for up to 3 days. Stir before serving to redistribute the dressing.
